advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the `total_needs == 0` best-effort push behind `not dry_run` so `--dry-run` never pushes.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:336:     if total_needs == 0:
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:338:         _best_effort_push(tracker, no_commit)
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:341:     if dry_run:

The workflow exposes `dry_run` via workflow_dispatch (.github/workflows/compact-sweep.yml:138 `if [ "${DRY_RUN}" = "true" ]; then ARGS+=(--dry-run); fi`), so an operator dry-run against an already-converged store would push.
advisory.finding: `compact_all_cli` performs a real push on `--dry-run` when there is nothing to compact: the `total_needs == 0` branch calls `_best_effort_push(tracker, no_commit)` before the `if dry_run` guard, so a dry-run invocation with zero selected tickets pushes the tickets branch (a side effect a dry-run must not have).
scenarios: Operator triggers the Compaction Sweep with dry_run=true against a store where every ticket is already under threshold (total_needs==0): a git push fires despite --dry-run.
advisory.suggested_fix: Move the `if dry_run:` check above the `total_needs == 0` block, or gate the push: `if total_needs == 0: ...; if not dry_run: _best_effort_push(tracker, no_commit); return 0`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the fail-closed OptionalDependencyError re-raise from push_after_commit is intended on the no-op/best-effort push path, or catch it there.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/push.py:742:     except OptionalDependencyError:
src/rebar/_store/push.py:746:         raise
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:291:     from rebar._store import push
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:293:     push.push_after_commit(tracker)
advisory.finding: `_best_effort_push` (and `_commit_backfill`'s push) call `push.push_after_commit`, whose docstring states it re-raises `OptionalDependencyError` (fail-closed on a misconfigured S3 remote); `_best_effort_push`'s own docstring frames it purely as a best-effort push, so a misconfigured remote turns a housekeeping sweep that folded nothing into a hard failure — worth confirming this is the intended posture for the no-op push path.
scenarios: S3 remote configured but boto3 absent: a sweep that folds nothing now raises out of _best_effort_push instead of quietly no-opping.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_two_independent_folds_of_one_ticket_converge actually merge clone_a's and clone_b's folds into a single store (git fetch+merge) and reduce the merged result, asserting the comment set is unchanged with no loss/duplication.
evidence: docstring: "Fold the ticket in two separate clones, then merge both back. The store must still reduce to the same ticket"
module docstring: "double-snapshot race — two clones fold the same ticket independently and both land; the merged store still reduces to the same ticket state, with no event lost or duplicated"
module docstring: "invariant I9 is the claim being tested here: a fold adds one SNAPSHOT and renames its sources to ``*.retired`` ... so the two merge as a union"

Test body (lines 101-117) folds in clone_a and clone_b, then asserts each clone independently reduces to `before` — no git merge/pull/fetch of clone_b's fold into clone_a (or into the source store) ever occurs. ABSENCE: the union-merge of two landed SNAPSHOTs is never constructed.
advisory.finding: test_two_independent_folds_of_one_ticket_converge does not merge the two clones' independent folds into one store, so the I9 union-merge convergence its docstring claims to test ('both land; the merged store still reduces to the same ticket state') is never exercised — it only re-verifies single-fold correctness in each clone separately.
advisory.suggested_fix: After both clones fold, push/fetch one clone's tickets branch into the other (or into a third store) via a git merge, then reduce the merged ticket dir and assert `_comment_bodies(state) == before`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives compact_all_cli down a folds-nothing (or nothing-to-do) path with push_after_commit monkeypatched, asserting it is invoked exactly once.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:286 docstring: "a sweep that folds nothing would silently skip the push — so the two are decoupled"
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:390-393: `if compacted > 0 and not no_commit: _commit_backfill(...) else: _best_effort_push(tracker, no_commit)`
test_a_pass_that_folds_nothing_is_not_counted_as_compacted (folds-nothing branch) asserts only `'0 compacted' in out` and `'nothing to fold' in out` — never that push occurred.

tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py:171 test_compact_all_keeps_the_legacy_best_effort_push_contract seeds one comment and lets the fold+commit path push; it does not cover a run that folds nothing.
ABSENCE: `search_files _best_effort_push` in tests returns no matches; no test drives the nothing-to-do or folds-nothing branch while asserting push_after_commit fires.
advisory.finding: The new best-effort push on paths that commit nothing (_best_effort_push at compact.py:338 and the folds-nothing else branch at 393) is untested: no test asserts push_after_commit is invoked when a sweep folds nothing, which is the exact regression the decoupling was introduced to prevent.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_a_pass_that_folds_nothing_is_not_counted_as_compacted, monkeypatch rebar._store.push.push_after_commit to record calls and assert it was called once (respecting --no-commit opt-out in a sibling case).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `timeout-minutes` bound to the compact-sweep job (matching reconcile-bridge.yml's convention) so a slow/stuck sweep cannot run to the 6-hour default.
evidence: compact-sweep.yml:50-55 defines the `sweep` job with `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and job-level `permissions` but no `timeout-minutes`
The workflow's own header cites cost: "held the ONE store write lock for the whole fold — measured at 13m53s on one close" (compact-sweep.yml:5-7)
Sibling scheduled workflows all bound themselves: reconcile-bridge.yml:80 `timeout-minutes: 60`, _mutation.yml:87 `timeout-minutes: 30`, reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:73 `timeout-minutes: 10`
`concurrency: {group: compact-sweep, cancel-in-progress: false}` (compact-sweep.yml:43-45) queues but does not cap wall-clock, so a stuck run holds the slot
advisory.finding: The scheduled compact-sweep job declares no `timeout-minutes`, so it inherits GitHub's 6-hour default while every other scheduled/long-running workflow in this repo bounds itself; a sweep that stalls or fans out over many over-threshold tickets can run unbounded and collide with the next 6-hourly schedule.
scenarios: A store with hundreds of over-threshold tickets makes the serial fold+push loop run for hours on a hosted runner
A hung git push/network step leaves the job burning billed minutes up to the 6h ceiling
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `timeout-minutes: 60` (or a value sized to the expected fold count) at the job level of `jobs.sweep`, alongside `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`.
